content: The following references provide detailed insights into various aspects of tuberculosis (TB) and its management, particularly in the context of HIV co-infection, pediatric care, drug resistance, and public health strategies: 1. Weekly administration of rifapentine and isoniazid was studied by the Tuberculosis Trials Consortium and published in The Lancet in 1999, highlighting its potential in TB treatment regimens. 2. Small PM, Shafer RW, Hopewell PC, and colleagues investigated exogenous reinfection with multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in patients with advanced HIV infection, as reported in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1993. 3. Crampin AC, Mwaungulu JN, and others examined whether recurrent TB in a general population cohort in Malawi was due to relapse or reinfection, with a focus on the impact of HIV, published in AIDS in 2010. 4. Narayanan S, Swaminathan S, and colleagues explored the influence of HIV infection on TB recurrence in South India, as detailed in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010. 5. Chaisson RE and Churchyard GJ reviewed the mechanisms of recurrent TB, including relapse and reinfection, in the context of HIV, as published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010. 6. Naidoo K and Dookie N provided insights into the risk factors associated with recurrent TB, distinguishing between relapse and reinfection, as part of a broader discussion on TB management. 7. Updated guidelines for the programmatic management of latent TB infection were consolidated by the World Health Organization (WHO) and accessed in March 2022. 8. The role of interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) as blood tests for TB infection was emphasized in WHO guidelines, accessed in December 2021. 9. Getahun H, Matteelli A, Chaisson RE, and Raviglione M discussed latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015. 10. Salgame P, Geadas C, Collins L, and colleagues revisited and revised concepts surrounding latent TB infection in Tuberculosis (Edinburgh) in 2015. 11. Schwoebel V, Koura KG, Adjibimey M, and others studied TB contact investigation and short-course preventive therapy among young children in Africa, as published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2020. 12. A WHO meeting reviewed the optimization of pediatric anti-TB drug formulations, with findings accessed in December 2021. 13. Becerra MC, Huang CC, Lecca L, and colleagues conducted a prospective cohort study on the transmissibility and disease progression potential of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, published in BMJ in 2019. 14. Marks SM, Mase SR, and Morris SB performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the cost-effectiveness of treating latent TB to prevent progression to multidrug-resistant TB, as reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2017. 15. The WHO operational handbook on TB diagnosis and treatment, including rapid diagnostic tools, was updated in 2021 and accessed in December 2021. 16. The WHO consolidated guidelines on TB treatment, including drug-resistant TB management, were accessed in December 2021. 17. Chiang SS, Brooks MB, Jenkins HE, and others analyzed the concordance of drug-resistance profiles between individuals with drug-resistant TB and their household contacts, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2021. 18. Management strategies for drug-resistant TB in children were outlined in a field guide accessed in December 2021. 19. Jenkins HE, Yuen CM, Rodriguez CA, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on childhood TB mortality, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017. 20. Turkov A, Wills GA, Wobudeya E, and others evaluated shorter treatment regimens for non-severe TB in children in Africa and India, as reported in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022. 21. Graham SM, Grzemska M, and Gie RP discussed the rationale for a new fixed-dose combination for first-line TB treatment in children, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2015. 22. Donald PR, Maher D, Maritz JS, and Qazi S reviewed ethambutol dosage recommendations for children, as detailed in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2006. 23. The WHO case definitions for HIV surveillance and clinical staging of HIV-related diseases were revised and accessed in December 2021. 24. Guidelines on managing severe acute malnutrition in children were updated and accessed in March 2022. 25. The WHO operational handbook on TB management in children and adolescents was accessed in December 2021. 26. Schaaf HS, Marais BJ, Whitelaw A, and others reviewed culture-confirmed childhood TB cases in Cape Town, South Africa, as published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2007. 27. Wolzak NK, Cooke ML, Orth H, and van Toorn R examined the changing profile of pediatric meningitis at a referral center in Cape Town, South Africa, as reported in Journal of Tropical Pediatrics in 2012. 28. Chiang SS, Khan FA, Milstein MB, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on childhood TB meningitis treatment outcomes, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014. 29. Van Toorn R, Schaaf HS, Laubscher JA, and others evaluated short intensified treatment regimens for children with drug-susceptible TB meningitis, as detailed in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2014. 30. Van Well GT, Paes BF, Terwee CB, and others conducted a retrospective cohort study on pediatric TB meningitis over 20 years in the Western Cape of South Africa, as published in Pediatrics in 2009. 31. Rapid advice on TB treatment in children was provided by the WHO and accessed in March 2022. 32. Donald PR reviewed chemotherapy for TB meningitis in children and adults, as published in Tuberculosis (Edinburgh) in 2010. 33. Guidelines for managing TB in children were published by the Department of Health in Pretoria in 2013. 34. A statement on child-friendly fixed-dose combinations for TB treatment in children was accessed in March 2022. 35. Lessons from the STEP-TB Project on childhood TB treatment pathways were accessed in December 2021. 36. Prasad K, Singh MB, and Ryan H reviewed the use of corticosteroids in managing TB meningitis, as published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 37. 38. Essential nutrition actions for TB patients were outlined in WHO guidelines accessed in March 2022. 39. Saukkonen JJ, Cohn DL, Jasmer RM, and others issued an official ATS statement on the hepatotoxicity of anti-TB therapy, as published in American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2006. 40. Guidelines for treating drug-susceptible TB and patient care were updated in 2017 and accessed in March 2022. 41. The WHO expert consultation on drug-resistant TB treatment outcome definitions was reported in November 2020. 42. Nahid P, Dorman SE, Alipanah N, and others provided clinical practice guidelines for treating drug-susceptible TB, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 43. Jenkins HE, Tolman AW, Yuen CM, and colleagues estimated the global incidence of multidrug-resistant TB in children, as reported in The Lancet in 2014. 44. Harauz E, Garcia-Prats AJ, Law S, and others reviewed treatment outcomes in children with multidrug-resistant TB, as published in PLOS Medicine in 2018. 45. Seddon JA, Hesseling AC, Godfrey-Faussett P, and Schaaf HS reported high treatment success rates in children treated for multidrug-resistant TB, as detailed in Thorax in 2014. 46. Shah NS, Yuen CM, Heo M, and others conducted a systematic review on contact investigations in households of patients with drug-resistant TB, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014. 47. Ettehad D, Schaaf HS, Seddon JA, and others reviewed treatment outcomes for children with multidrug-resistant TB, as reported in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2012. 48. Garcia-Prats AJ, Schaaf HS, Hesseling AC, and others studied the pharmacokinetics and safety of linezolid in children with multidrug-resistant TB, as published in PLOS Medicine in 2019. 49. Challenges in using new and repurposed drugs for treating multidrug-resistant TB in children were discussed by Schaaf HS, Garcia-Prats AJ, McKenna L, and Seddon JA in Expert Review of Clinical Pharmacology in 2018. 50. The WHO operational handbook on TB management in children and adolescents was accessed in December 2021.
